newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rise at open after U.S. PPI data.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rise at open after U.S. PPI data.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 19875.49 +120.71 LME CASH NICKEL US$6750 -20.0
CANDLR 1.3700 LME CASH ALUM US$1537.5 -13.5
CAN 30-YR 118.48 +0.19 BRENT CRUDE US$18.01 +0.05
* Toronto stocks rose at the open on Friday after U.S. PPI data came in slightly weaker than expected. * 10.3 million shares traded worth C$103 million. * 232 advances, 180 declines, 202 flat.
Toronto stocks ticked higher at the open on Friday, passing Thursday's record close and inching toward the exchange's life-time intra-session high of 6615.
"The market opened a little bit firmer here today," one trader said.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 8.01 to 6600.93 in turnover of 10.3 million shares worth C$103 million. Advancing stocks outpaced declines 232 to 180, while 202 issues were unchanged. The trader said stronger steels helped boost the industrial subgroup, and paper and forest issues remained popular.

"(Dofasco Inc ) stock is up another dollar today, trading at 31.80...(Stelco Inc STE.TO ) is better, trading at 11.70. It did tick up as high as 11.85, so that seems to be one of the stocks that does have momentum to it," the trader said.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes rose, led by industrial products, which gained 56.59 points or 1.2 percent to 4788.79.
Paper and forest products rose 35.66 points or 0.56 percent to 5375.86, extending a rally that began early this week with the restructuring at U.S.-based International Paper Co.

The oil group struggled for the second day, shedding 35.66 points or 0.52 percent to 6848.87. Renaissance Energy Ltd lost 0.70 to 35.40 in early trade of just under 200,000 shares after the company said yesterday it "screwed up big time" by not warning sooner that its crude oil production would be lower than expected in 1997.
The trader said weaker than expected U.S. PPI data this morning helped the bank group move higher in early trade but otherwise had little impact on the market.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* Shares in Geac Computer Corp Ltd rose 7.55 to 45.55 in healthy trade after it announced fourth-quarter earnings of C$0.70 a share, up 131 percent from the C$0.31 per share profit reported in the same period last year.

* Shares in iStar internet inc dropped 0.53 to 2.62 in turnover of more than 175,000 shares after the struggling company said on Thursday it struck a deal with Bell Canada that gives iStar C$20-million worth of Bell services in return for a possible future stake in the Internet company. The stock price gyrated earlier this week on rumors of the deal.

* Shares in Air Canada rose 0.45 to 11.25 in turnover of almost 300,000 shares after news that it and other members of the recently launched Star Alliance met on Thursday in Frankfurt, Germany to discuss whether to establish a global cargo alliance.
